Problem: Denali 16 dogs, Nate 12 dogs. They will be assigned/unassigned new dogs in groups of x dogs. The ratio of Denali's pay to Nate's pay would be the same if Denali started walking 4x more dogs and Nate stayed at 12 dogs OR if x of Nate's dogs were reassigned to Denali. Find x (x≠0).

Interpretation: Pay proportional to number of dogs walked. Ratio Denali:Nate = dogs_D / dogs_N.

Scenario A: Denali walks 4x more dogs (i.e., adds 4x to his count) and Nate stays at 12. So Denali dogs = 16 + 4x, Nate = 12. Ratio = (16+4x)/12.

Scenario B: x of Nate's dogs are reassigned to Denali. So Denali gets +x, Nate loses x. Denali = 16 + x, Nate = 12 - x. Ratio = (16+x)/(12 - x).

Set equal: (16+4x)/12 = (16+x)/(12 - x). Solve.

Cross-multiply: (16+4x)*(12 - x) = 12*(16+x).

Compute left: (16+4x)*(12 - x) = 16*12 -16*x +4x*12 -4x*x = 192 -16x +48x -4x^2 = 192 +32x -4x^2.

Right
